Define the model

Source: R/model_spec.R
define_model.Rd

Declares the goals of the preemptive goal program (Rocha, 2026, section 4.4): the satellite accounts (in declaration order), the direction and the goal of each one, the economic block (ECO), the priority orderings, the scenarios and the use of the corridor declared with the data.

Usage

define_model(
  accounts,
  economy = list(direction = ">=", target = "final_demand"),
  priorities = "all",
  scenarios = NULL,
  corridor = list(use = TRUE, multiplier = 1),
  lock_tolerance = "auto",
  name = "model",
  data = NULL,
  max_orderings = 720
)

Arguments

accounts

Named list, one entry per satellite account, in declaration order. Each entry: direction, target and, optionally, weight, unit and label.

economy

List with direction (default ">="), target ("final_demand", the default, the declared f; a numeric vector with one goal per sector; or a CSV file with code and value), position ("last", the default, or "free") and deviation ("absolute", the default, or "relative").

priorities

"all", a permute specification or a list of explicit orderings (see above).

scenarios

Named list of scenarios (optional).

corridor

List with use (default TRUE) and multiplier (default 1).

lock_tolerance

Lock of the levels already solved. "auto" (default): the exact lock d_l == Z_l and, only if a level of the run ends non-optimal (a false infeasibility of GLPK), the run is solved again with relaxed locks d_l <= Z_l + t * max(1, |Z_l|), with the smallest t among 1e-12, 1e-11, 1e-10 and 1e-9 that makes every level optimal. Runs that are optimal with the exact lock do not change; each run records the tolerance used, and the outputs flag the relaxed runs. "exact" (or 0): only the exact lock. A number t (up to 1e-6): the exact lock and, if it fails, the relaxed one with t.

name

Name of the model (used in the outputs).

data

Path of the database (optional; used by run_model() when the model comes from a file).

max_orderings

Safety limit for the number of orderings.

Value

Object of class lexio_model.

Details

Directions. ">=" (a floor: the goal should be reached or exceeded) penalizes d-; "<=" (a ceiling: the goal should not be exceeded) penalizes d+; "=" penalizes both. The direction is declared for each account; in Rocha (2026), the entrant energy is ">=", the incumbent energy "<=" and labour ">=".

Goals of the satellite accounts (b = base of the account, D x):

  • list(type = "base"): keep the base, g = b;

  • list(type = "growth", rate = r): g = b + b * r;

  • list(type = "pooled_share", share = s, pool = c("A", "B")): g = b + (b_A + b_B) * s, a shock equal to a share of the sum of the bases of a set of accounts;

  • list(type = "delta", value = v): g = b + v;

  • list(type = "level", value = v): g = v.

Priorities. Each priority level minimizes the weighted sum of the penalized deviations of its goals; the levels are solved in order, each one locked at its optimum (preemptive priorities). Without a declaration, every ordering is run; to run only some orderings, declare them.

  • "all" (default): one level per account, all k! orders of the accounts in lexicographic order of declaration (with 3 accounts, P1 = 1-2-3, P2 = 1-3-2, P3 = 2-1-3, P4 = 2-3-1, P5 = 3-1-2, P6 = 3-2-1).

  • list(permute = list(c("OIL", "COAL"), c("SO2", "HC"), "EMP")): all orders of the declared groups (a group is one level with several goals).

  • A list of explicit orderings, each a list of levels, for instance list(first = c("GC", "GD", "LAB"), second = list(c("GD", "GC"), "LAB")). Only these orderings are run. Each account appears exactly once; an ordering given as a character vector has one level per element.

ECO is fixed at the last level (the benchmark of the model: it absorbs the final impact). To place it elsewhere, the operator must say so explicitly with economy = list(position = "free"): then "ECO" can be written at any level of an explicit ordering, and with "all" or permute ECO enters the permutations ((k + 1)! orderings with "all"). With position = "last" (default), "ECO" may be written only as the last level, and it is added there when omitted.

Economic deviations. With economy = list(deviation = "absolute") (default), the ECO level minimizes the sum of the deviations of the sectors in currency units, so large sectors weigh more. With deviation = "relative", each sector's deviation is divided by its goal, d_h / |g_h|: the level minimizes the sum of the proportional deviations, and a shortfall of 1% weighs the same in every sector. It needs g_h != 0 in every sector.

Weights. weight (default 1) multiplies the deviation of an account inside its level; it only matters when several goals share a level.

Corridor. The corridor itself is declared with the data (declare_io()). corridor = list(use = FALSE) ignores it (free model); multiplier scales alpha.

Scenarios. Each scenario replaces the goals of some accounts and, optionally, the directions (directions) and the corridor (corridor). Without scenarios, the model has one scenario, main.

See also

read_model(), run_model().

Examples

shock <- list(type = "pooled_share", share = 0.05, pool = c("E", "I"))
m <- define_model(list(
  E = list(direction = ">=", target = shock),
  I = list(direction = "<=", target = "base"),
  LAB = list(direction = ">=", target = list(type = "growth", rate = 0.05))
))
m
#> <lexio_model> model | 3 satellite account(s), 1 scenario(s), 6 priority ordering(s) | lock: auto (exact; relaxed only where GLPK fails) 
#>   E        >= base + 0.05 x (E + I)
#>   I        <= base
#>   LAB      >= base x (1 + 0.05)
#>   ECO      >= final demand f | absolute deviations | fixed at the last level
#>   corridor: as declared in the data (multiplier 1) 
#>   P01: E > I > LAB > ECO
#>   P02: E > LAB > I > ECO
#>   P03: I > E > LAB > ECO
#>   P04: I > LAB > E > ECO
#>   P05: LAB > E > I > ECO
#>   P06: LAB > I > E > ECO
#>   scenario main
